results: Reference taxonomy includes active input options, legacy filter options and campus time
Lost creation persists four public/two private photos, NULL time, history and notifications
Found creation persists rule-based matches and clear suggestion state on both reports
Search/category/location/type/status/date, literal characters and paging are SQL-backed
Public API/photos omit ownership data; BM-only evidence and direct storage guards hold
Server field/date/time/active category/location boundaries reject without partial records
Server upload independently rejects MIME/dimensions/size/count and Found ownership photos
Own edit retains/replaces media; combined limits and foreign photo IDs are enforced
Controlled metadata failure rolls back new report/history/notifs and removes new files
Eligible delete cascades metadata/files, retains NULL notification refs and updates suggestions
Valid ownership claim links own Lost, keeps evidence private and locks related edits
Duplicate and concurrent same-user claims create exactly one active record
Request-more-info resubmit reuses ID, preserves selected evidence, replaces only after commit
Controlled failure after claim file save rolls back claim/item/history/notifs and files
Terminal items/Lost links and approved claims are not eligible; suggestions stay suggestions
Time/location legacy read/filter and own notifications are persisted and isolated
Approved/ready-pickup reports reject renewed claims and show only authorized pickup records
Browser Lost form validates and uploads prepared public/private photos with gallery and NULL time
Browser Found report switches fields, uploads and appears in searchable discovery cards
Browser claim and NEED_MORE_INFO resubmit preserve ID, answer/Lost link and explicit evidence
Browser failed save retains draft; upload invalid formats/size are explained and retry works
Own activity cards and delete confirmation cancel/commit behave without a wide table
Notifications persist read state before claim link; history cards are read-only and empty states useful
All seven Student pages are responsive and usable at all five required viewports
